papers.title: Complications Encountered with Total Hip Arthroplasty in Rheumatoid Patients
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis affects around 1% of the global population with a predilection for Western societies. The treatment of the rheumatoid hip has gone through significant changes in recent years. Although osteotomies and synovectomies were previously commonplace, advances in arthroplasty technique and technology has seen these former procedures being performed less commonly. This article tackles some of the key issues with regard to the rheumatoid hip, namely the increased risk and methods of dealing with protrusio acetabuli, the risk of dislocation, infection and rates of aseptic loosening.

summary_en.motivation: To review the specific complications and management strategies for total hip arthroplasty in patients with rheumatoid arthritis.
summary_en.method: A narrative review synthesizing previous clinical studies and surgical experience.
summary_en.result: Rheumatoid hips carry higher risks of protrusio acetabuli, dislocation, infection, and aseptic loosening.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; based on clinical literature and expert opinion.
